cards.explanation: The answer is Himself. The text says God "…had no one greater to swear by…" so "…He swore by Himself…" (Hebrews 6:13). Nobody sits above Him, so He put His own name behind the promise. Friends, that's about as solid as a promise gets.

The answer is that God would bless Abraham and give him many descendants. God said, "I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants." (Hebrews 6:14). Blessing and a whole lot of family. I think Abraham was going to need a bigger dinner table.

The answer is patiently. "…after waiting patiently, obtained the promise." (Hebrews 6:15). Abraham didn't grab it early. He waited, and then he got it. Bakers, I'd have been checking the oven every four seconds.

The answer is that the oath ends all argument. The writer says an oath "…serves as a confirmation to end all argument." (Hebrews 6:16). When someone swears by someone greater, the matter is settled. Picture a family debate over the last cookie finally ending. That's the idea.

The answer is unchanging. God wanted to make "…the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise…" (Hebrews 6:17). His purpose doesn't shift around, friends. He guaranteed it with an oath so they could see it.

The answer is lie. The text says it is "…impossible for God to lie…" (Hebrews 6:18). God made a promise to Abraham and guaranteed it with an oath (Hebrews 6:13, 17). Those are the two unchangeable things. That's a solid base for everyone to stand on.

The answer is True. The text says that by these two unchangeable things, "…we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged." (Hebrews 6:18). Strong encouragement is what those two things give, friends.
The answer is firm and secure. "We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure." (Hebrews 6:19). An anchor that wobbled wouldn't be much use, bakers. This one holds.
The answer is Jesus. Hebrews says "…Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf." (Hebrews 6:20). He went in first, for us. That's what a forerunner does, friends.
The answer is False. Jesus "…has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek." (Hebrews 6:20). It isn't for a set time, bakers. There's no end date on it. Forever means forever.
